title: Joy in Adversity
paragraphs: The hero elopes with the heroine, bound by the spell of love. Their journey extends from the sylvan tract through the arid wastes. This is a scene from Kalittokai, seen in the backdrop of Tolkāppiyam.

In the early morning, being parted from the mother, she accompanies her lover by holding his hand. She comes across deer and rabbit frolicking among koṉṟai, kāyā and kuruntam trees. Blossoms of mullai, kullai and paṭavam are spreading fragrance all around. The peasants rush to sow common millets like cāmai and varaku. She beholds all the scenes while continuing the journey.

Since the dawn replaces early morning darkness, they can no longer remain hidden from others. The twinkling stars scattered profusely on the sky gravitate us to see them. Even among those innumerable stars, don’t we view the moon first? This most beautiful damsel is that moon! She is like a statue in beauty! She moves like an exquisite art! When she goes along with her lover equally matching in charm and valour, nobody could miss an opportunity to admire that perfect pair.

When they travel a long distance in the desert land, they are trailed by the foster mother, anxious to trace them. In that land, where are seen emaciated elephants and wolves moving around and parched ponds and wells, the foster mother travels listening to the music of the paṟai (a percussion instrument) and the yāḻ (a stringed musical instrument) even while she eagerly enquires about her daughter and her lover.
“Mother, why are you treading the fearsome path looking for them? We saw both of them. Our village is nearby, you can take a sojourn in our place’. As we

said thus, they stayed with us for a while and resumed their journey towards a far-off village.” Though the news conveyed by the residents of that hamlet tastes like honey, her daughter’s separation stings her like a scorpion.

“Mother, we could appreciate your position. Being a mother, you are delighted to hear about their wellbeing; so it is only fitting on your part to facilitate their marriage and thereby be more happy”. Thus saying they try to restrain the mother:

> The patterns of utterance > Enjoined on those > Who meet on the way > The lovers in elopement are: > Warning the hero and heroine on elopement > Against the perilous nature of their journey > At such a time and along such a tract > As would be wrought with fright; > Telling them through words of kindness and concern > To stay in the village nearby > Since their destination stands removed afar; > Exhorting the couple united in love > Through words of compassion > Against the course of deed they took to; > Forbidding the foster-mother to pursue the lovers > As she has set out in search of them; > Guiding the foster-mother’s pursuit of the lovers; > Speaking of the long distance the lovers traversed, > And speaking of the return of the lovers, > So goes the norm of utterance types in Akam poetry. > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verse 40).
“Is it a far-off place? Doesn’t matter. I will retrieve my daughter by treading the turbulent path, however difficult the journey might be”. The mother vows and starts off.

Isn’t it a mother’s heart? It would naturally be tumultuous. Though she has learnt of her daughter’s wellbeing, she desires that the girl should stay in her parental protection. Otherwise, the efforts to nourish her so long would vanish into the thin air. So saying, the frustrated mother runs towards the direction where
the lovers are supposed to have gone.

The sun is scorching. On the way, she is encountered by some sage men treading the desert path. She discloses her predicament to them. “Have you seen my daughter along with a broad-shouldered man?” so saying she trembles in anxiety.
“We did see them, mother. The flag of love flies aloft in their hearts. Don’t think of cutting it off, mother.”
“What are you saying? When her own mother and me, her foster-mother, are grieving thus, is it proper for you to support the girl who has gone away to our grief?”

“Mother, listen! Though sweet-smelling sandal sprouts and grows in the mountain, it doesn’t belong to the mountain. It is meant for applying on the body. Being born in water, can the pearl remain wedded to the water? It will add to the beauty of the one who wears it. The music emanating from the yāḻ gives pleasure not to the yāḻ but to the auditors or the one who plays it. Mother, your daughter is like sandal born from the mountain, pearl born from the sea, music from the yāḻ. Therefore, it is best for her to be with her loved man.” Here is that Kalittokai poem:

> Not unseen by us they were, > We did see them tread this torrid path; > You seem to be the mother of that maid > Decked in grace with resplendent ornaments, > Who this desert path braved > With a youth of quintessential bearing. > > On reflection we see that > Your daughter is to you > What the fragrant sandal mixed with myriad things > Is to the mountain where it’s born; > It’s beneficial to those only who apply it on them. > > On pondering it we find that > Your daughter is to you > What the choice white pearl is to the ocean > Where it’s born; > It serves those only who wear it on them. > > Weighing it right we find that
> Your daughter is to you > What the enchanting melody, > The seven strings in unison issue, > Is to the yāḻ where it’s conceived; > It’s beneficial to the songsters only.

The lover and his love after surmounting the difficult problems settle down in life. Realizing that they were leading a virtuous life, the foster-mother abandoned her search. It is natural that she would visit them, stay with them and attain heartfelt pleasure. Such would be the collective essence of Tolkāppiyam Poruḷatikāram and Kalittokai.
